claim: The F# capital model reproduces agent AB's S3 cash and fully loaded cost to first referenceable invoice exactly; Revision 2 adds the governing M1 registry, Nacha TPSP obligations, funded control operations, a realistic first conversion and go-live lag, and roughly doubles the base cash to first invoice (data/model-outputs/tables/key-figures.md)

Phase II ER-7 charges full burn during build months while the burn includes the platform team that builds; at a 40% build-phase run ER-7 base capital falls by about $1M (data/model-outputs/tables/phase2-double-count.md)
notes: Confirms P3-CLM-AB004 from the code (Routes.fs adds Build/buildMonths to Burn every build month)

claim: ER-7's 0.30 variable share applied to revenue already net of a 30% channel share is a partial double count: it raises vendor variable cost per account above the direct route's although the partner carries first-line support; the per-account-equivalent share is 0.214, not AB's 0.15
notes: Resolves P3-CLM-AB005 (hypothesized) from code and inputs; the input basis documents no partner-specific cost

claim: GAP-HI010: Phase II operating modes MD-3..MD-7 already carry registry engineering (platform team and charity-data subscriptions, PR #87 layer B) and price vetting labour in EV-E08; adding registry run cost to them double counts. Agent AB's lean licensor run carries no registry, so it must be added there
Agent AB's staged self-sufficiency script charges implementation only for the first customer; later customers need $10-80k each (AB's own S6 range), which the corrected model adds

With the DAF cost center opened at month 0 the kill rule pauses every platform sequence at month 24 under both bases; with a whole first signing and a go-live lag of 8 months or less, or with the cost center opened at month 6 or later (as the P3-DEC-MOD003 gate would), A3 passes; the result is timing-sensitive (data/model-outputs/tables/kill-timing.md)

Under the revision-3 (CFO-corrected) basis a sequence pays back within 120 months only if Echelon does not perform the human deep review (sponsor-performed, P3-DEC-MOD005) or OD-CDD-02 allows M5, and then only the partner-book sequence pays back in base; single-sponsor A3 is held back by the small plausible-sponsor population (data/model-outputs/tables/bases.md)
notes: Revision 3 (REV4019, REV4008); revision 2 found no payback in any configuration

claim: Summing savings claimed by the event model (EV-E08) and the registry model on the same vetting labour exceeds the labour itself; sequential residual accounting avoids it (data/model-outputs/tables/events-double-count.md)

The shared-infrastructure share Unbound bears depends entirely on the allocation rule (0.25-0.98 of the pooled assurance and infrastructure cost in base); under a revenue rule Unbound bears almost all of it until a second product earns revenue (data/model-outputs/tables/shared-infra.md)
notes: Agent AB's S7 factor 0.6 is one point inside this range

claim: For a completed Unbound under the governing registry mode, peak cash is most sensitive to charities in use per account, variable cost per account, the registry mode itself and the partner share; build cost is a minor driver (data/model-outputs/tables/tornado-sequence-a3.md)

Customer funding no longer lowers peak cash for partner-delivered sequences (the partner bills and remits), and partner funding raises it (the extra share costs more than it pays); funding routes change who carries the deficit, not whether one exists (data/model-outputs/tables/sequences-funding.md)

Outside investment is not shown to be necessary or useful before the gate: in every basis and configuration the kill rule pauses at month 24 with about $1.3-1.8M spent, and payback exists only for the partner book under sponsor-performed review or M5; capital beyond the cash at risk before the first test is not justified until a named partner and the review allocation are settled (P3-GAP-MOD001)

A lean licensor's walk-away net price remains below Phase II MD-6's after funded control operations, TPSP obligations and the M1 registry are added, but the lean structure does not survive channel loss or the registry review cost at governing scope (data/model-outputs/tables/response-walk-away.md)
notes: Revision 2: REV1004, REV3005; conditional on P3-ASM-AB030 sponsor size

claim: With the human 180-day full review (M1), the registry for the first sponsors costs more per licensed account than the net licence price at the Phase II reference price, and break-even then needs sponsors larger than almost any in the FY2024 panel; OD-CDD-02 (automated renewal) is therefore a precondition for a licensing business, not an efficiency gain (data/model-outputs/tables/break-even-revenue.md)
notes: REV3010; REV3020; per-account registry cost depends on charities in use per account (P3-ASM-HI030)

claim: Few FY2024 sponsors are plausible single-sponsor customers: excluding donation processors and national sponsors presumed to run their own platforms leaves 17 sponsors with at least 2,646 accounts and 10 with at least 5,291; a partner's book is the larger addressable unit (data/model-outputs/tables/platform-classes.md)

Building the remaining S2-to-S3 scope outside the DAF cost center (A3X) moves the build off the kill-rule clock without reducing it; under the rule it lets more cash be spent before the first pause than building inside the cost center (A3B) (data/model-outputs/tables/sequences-kill-rule.md)

Charging the human deep review to Echelon is structurally loss-making once each sponsor's reliance is kept separate: with Echelon performing M1 reviews no single-sponsor or partner-book size below 100,000 accounts breaks even; with the sponsor performing them (DEC-006 licensing; r1 sponsor policy) single-sponsor break-even falls to about 3,000 accounts (data/model-outputs/tables/gate-break-even.md)

Revision 2 over-stated cost (perpetual contingency on run, union-shared deep review twice a year, control-operations overlap) and under-stated demand constraints (population cap counting processors and captive sponsors, cumulative cap); the decision to gate DAF-specific spend on a named partner does not depend on which basis is used (data/model-outputs/tables/bases.md)
